nodes.title: Microsoft Intune: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Intune is Microsoft's cloud-based endpoint management service for mobile device management (MDM) and mobile application management (MAM), unifying device and app control through the Microsoft Intune admin center. The MD-102 and MS-102 exams test enrollment, compliance, configuration profiles, app protection, and Conditional Access integration.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a compliance policy and a configuration profile in Intune?
flashcards.back: A compliance policy defines rules a device must meet (encryption, OS version, no jailbreak) and reports a compliant/non-compliant state; a configuration profile pushes actual settings (Wi-Fi, VPN, restrictions, certificates) onto the device. Compliance evaluates, configuration enforces settings.

flashcards.front: What does an app protection policy (APP/MAM) protect without requiring device enrollment?
flashcards.back: It protects data inside managed apps at the app level — controlling cut/copy/paste, save-as, encryption, and PIN access to corporate data — so it works on unenrolled BYOD devices (MAM-without-enrollment).

flashcards.front: How does Intune compliance integrate with Conditional Access?
flashcards.back: Intune reports each device's compliance state to Microsoft Entra ID; a Conditional Access policy can then require a compliant (or Entra hybrid-joined) device before granting access to apps like Exchange or SharePoint, blocking non-compliant devices.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of device enrollment in Intune?
flashcards.back: Enrollment registers a device with Intune so it can receive MDM management — applying policies, profiles, and apps. Methods include Windows Autopilot, Apple Automated Device Enrollment (ADE), and Android Enterprise enrollment.

questions.q: Contoso ships brand-new corporate laptops directly from the OEM to remote employees. Each laptop must boot to Windows 11, prompt the user for their Microsoft 365 credentials, automatically join Microsoft Entra ID, enroll in Intune, and receive all required apps before the desktop appears. Which Windows deployment approach should you use?
choices: Provisioning packages built in Windows Configuration Designer and copied to a USB drive shipped with each laptop
A Microsoft Configuration Manager OSD task sequence triggered by PXE boot on the corporate network
Windows Autopilot user-driven deployment with an Enrollment Status Page that blocks the user until required apps complete
A custom Windows image deployed by the OEM with a first-boot setup script that joins the device manually
questions.explanation: Windows Autopilot is purpose-built for the zero-touch, OEM-shipped scenario. The user-driven deployment profile triggers Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment from the OOBE, and an Enrollment Status Page (ESP) gates the desktop until required apps and policies finish installing. Provisioning packages require the user to plug in a USB stick and only set local configuration — they do not stream apps or block the OOBE. ConfigMgr OSD needs PXE/network boot on a corporate LAN, which remote shipping precludes. A custom OEM image bypasses the modern provisioning flow and leaves enrollment and app delivery to ad-hoc scripts.

questions.q: You configure a Windows Autopilot user-driven profile and an Enrollment Status Page (ESP). Users report that when a required Win32 app fails to install the device falls through to the desktop anyway, which violates your security policy. Which ESP configuration must you change so that an installation failure blocks sign-in?
choices: Set 'Show app and profile configuration installation progress' to No so that a re-enrollment is forced on failure
Reduce the 'Time spent showing installation progress' from 60 minutes to 15 minutes so the user has less time to bypass the page
Set 'Only show page to devices provisioned by out-of-box experience (OOBE)' to No so the ESP also runs at every interactive sign-in
Set 'Block device use until all apps and profiles are installed' to Yes and configure the failure-action option so the 'Continue anyway' button is removed when an error occurs
questions.explanation: The setting that hard-stops the device on failure is 'Block device use until all apps and profiles are installed' combined with the failure-action toggle that suppresses the 'Continue anyway' button. Without those, the ESP only displays progress and falls through to the desktop when an app times out. Hiding the progress page entirely does not block usage; shortening the timeout makes failures more likely rather than more enforced; and disabling the OOBE-only scope just makes the ESP appear at every sign-in without changing how failures are handled.

questions.q: You manage 500 Windows 11 devices in Intune. Change control requires that any new Windows 11 feature update is held back on production devices for 60 days while a pilot ring validates it. Which Intune object enforces that deferral on the production ring?
choices: A feature update profile in Intune set to the desired Windows release version
A Windows update ring with 'Feature update deferral period (days)' set to 60, assigned to the production device group
A quality update profile in Intune configured with a 60-day deferral
A device compliance policy that marks devices non-compliant when a newer feature update is detected
questions.explanation: An update ring in Intune exposes 'Feature update deferral period (days)', which delays installation of new Windows feature updates by up to 365 days for the assigned devices — exactly the production-ring deferral the change board wants. Feature update profiles pin devices to a specific Windows release rather than deferring by a number of days. Quality update profiles cover monthly cumulative quality updates, not feature releases. Compliance policies report device state but do not control which updates are installed or when.

questions.q: Only Intune-managed laptops marked compliant should be allowed to access SharePoint Online. Personal devices must continue to reach Outlook on the web. Which combination correctly enforces this?
choices: A device compliance policy in Intune for Windows together with a Conditional Access policy that targets the SharePoint Online cloud app and requires the device to be marked as compliant
A device configuration profile delivered through Intune that blocks SharePoint when the device is not compliant
An app protection policy targeting the SharePoint mobile apps with 'Block access from unmanaged devices' enabled
A Microsoft Entra ID Protection user-risk policy that blocks high-risk sign-ins to SharePoint
questions.explanation: Conditional Access is the only enforcement surface that can scope access to a cloud app (SharePoint Online) based on device state, and the 'Require device to be marked as compliant' grant control depends on an Intune compliance policy evaluating the laptop. Device configuration profiles set settings on the device — they do not block cloud-app access. App protection policies protect data inside mobile apps on iOS/Android, not on corporate Windows laptops. An Entra ID Protection user-risk policy reacts to identity risk signals, not to device compliance state.

questions.q: You must disable the Microsoft Edge built-in password manager on all managed Windows 11 endpoints. Your team has standardized on the Settings catalog whenever a setting is available there. Which Intune profile should you create?
choices: An Administrative Templates profile and locate the Edge password manager policy under Computer Configuration
A Settings catalog profile, search for the Edge category, and set 'Enable saving passwords to the password manager' (PasswordManagerEnabled) to Disabled
A custom OMA-URI profile pointing to the Edge ADMX policy namespace
A device restrictions profile under the 'Microsoft Edge browser' settings group
questions.explanation: The Settings catalog exposes the full Microsoft Edge ADMX policy set — including PasswordManagerEnabled — as searchable, individually selectable settings, which matches the team standard. Administrative Templates is the older Intune surface and exposes only a curated subset of ADMX. Custom OMA-URI works but is the fallback used when the Settings catalog does not yet surface a policy. The 'Microsoft Edge browser' group inside device restrictions covers the legacy (EdgeHTML) browser, not modern Chromium-based Edge.

questions.q: You must deploy a 200-MB legacy line-of-business installer (setup.exe with several supporting files) to Windows devices via Intune. Which packaging step is required before you can upload the installer as a Win32 app?
choices: Sign the setup.exe with a code-signing certificate purchased from a public certificate authority
Re-package the installer as an MSIX bundle using the MSIX Packaging Tool
Convert the installer to a .appx package using Visual Studio
Run the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool (IntuneWinAppUtil.exe) against the source folder to produce a .intunewin file, then upload that file
questions.explanation: Intune Win32 apps must be uploaded as a .intunewin payload produced by the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool. The tool wraps the source folder containing setup.exe and any dependencies, compresses and encrypts the bundle, and outputs the .intunewin file the portal accepts. Code-signing is recommended but not a Win32 upload requirement. Repackaging to MSIX or .appx is a different deployment model entirely and is not needed simply to ship an existing setup.exe.

questions.q: Sales staff want to read corporate email and SharePoint files on their personal iPhones without enrolling the devices in Intune. Corporate data must be encrypted at rest inside the apps and removable on demand without wiping the user's personal data. Which Intune feature should you configure?
choices: A device compliance policy that targets unenrolled iOS devices
A device configuration profile delivered through Apple Configurator
An app protection policy (Mobile Application Management without enrollment) for the Office mobile apps, targeted to personal devices
A device restrictions profile that blocks copy and paste between apps
questions.explanation: App protection policies — also known as Mobile Application Management (MAM) without enrollment — protect corporate data inside supported apps such as Outlook, OneDrive, Teams and Word on devices that are not enrolled in Intune. They encrypt the corporate data containers, gate access with a PIN, and let an admin selectively wipe only the corporate data on demand. Compliance policies and device configuration profiles require an enrolled device. Apple Configurator is a device provisioning utility, not an Intune MAM control.

questions.q: You must silently enable BitLocker on the operating system drive of all corporate Windows 11 laptops and have the recovery key escrowed to Microsoft Entra ID before encryption begins. Which Intune profile should you create?
choices: Endpoint security → Disk encryption profile of type 'BitLocker', enabling silent enablement on the OS drive and selecting 'Back up recovery information to Azure AD before enabling BitLocker'
Endpoint security → Attack surface reduction profile with the rule 'Block credential stealing from the LSASS subsystem' enabled
Endpoint security → Account protection profile that requires Windows Hello for Business
Endpoint security → Firewall profile with an inbound rule that allows the BitLocker management snap-in
questions.explanation: BitLocker is configured under Endpoint security → Disk encryption. The BitLocker profile lets you require silent enablement on the operating system drive and escrow the recovery key to Microsoft Entra ID before encryption begins, satisfying both requirements in one policy. Attack surface reduction profiles tune Defender ASR rules; Account protection covers Windows Hello and local-account groups; Firewall profiles configure Windows Defender Firewall rules. None of those activate BitLocker.

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.

questions.q: Your security team wants to stop Office applications from creating child processes — a common phishing-payload technique — but they need a measurement period to see what would break before the rule is enforced. Which Intune endpoint security configuration should you apply?
choices: Set the attack surface reduction rule to Block immediately and add an exclusion for every Office app to soften the impact
Disable Microsoft Defender Tamper Protection during the measurement period so events surface in the event log
Configure a Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy in enforced mode that allows only Office processes
Set the attack surface reduction rule 'Block Office applications from creating child processes' to Audit mode on the targeted devices
questions.explanation: Each ASR rule supports modes including Block, Audit and Warn. Audit logs what the rule would have blocked without disrupting users, which is exactly the measurement the team is asking for — events appear in Defender for Endpoint and the Defender event log for review. Enforcing the rule defeats the measurement; excluding every Office app makes the rule meaningless; disabling Tamper Protection weakens Defender as a whole and is unrelated. WDAC in enforced mode is a far broader application-control surface than this single ASR rule.

questions.q: A new branch of a cloud-first company will deploy 50 freshly imaged Windows 11 laptops. There is no on-premises Active Directory and there are no plans to deploy one. Users sign in with Microsoft 365 cloud accounts. Which device join type should you target?
choices: Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, so that domain Group Policy continues to apply
Microsoft Entra registered (Workplace Join) so that the personal-style sign-in is preserved
Microsoft Entra joined, with management configured through Microsoft Intune
On-premises Active Directory domain joined via DirectAccess back to corporate headquarters
questions.explanation: With no on-premises AD and cloud-only identities, Microsoft Entra join is the correct path — the device is joined directly to Microsoft Entra ID and managed by Intune through MDM enrollment. Hybrid join requires an on-premises AD forest that the device first joins. Microsoft Entra registered is intended for personal BYOD devices and gives only single sign-on rather than corporate ownership and management. Joining a non-existent on-premises domain over DirectAccess is not feasible.

questions.q: A field laptop is being reassigned from a departing employee to a new one. Corporate apps, Wi-Fi profiles and the existing Intune enrollment must remain, but the previous user's accounts, data and personal settings must be removed without re-installing the OEM image. Which remote action should you run from Intune?
choices: Wipe — performs a factory reset and unenrolls the device
Autopilot Reset — removes personal data and settings but keeps the device Intune-enrolled and reapplies the assigned Autopilot deployment profile
Fresh Start — keeps user data and removes pre-installed OEM Win32 apps
Retire — removes corporate data and leaves user data intact
questions.explanation: Autopilot Reset is the action designed for reassignment: it removes user data, accounts and settings while preserving the device's Intune enrollment and reapplying the assigned Autopilot deployment profile, so corporate apps and policies return automatically for the new user. Wipe is a full factory reset and unenrollment, which would force the device through full provisioning again. Fresh Start removes pre-installed Win32 OEM apps but keeps user data — the opposite of the requirement. Retire is the MAM-side action that removes only corporate data on personally owned scenarios.

questions.q: Corporate policy states that personally-owned Android devices are not allowed to enroll in Intune; only corporate-owned Android Enterprise dedicated and fully managed devices may enroll. Which Intune feature enforces that boundary?
choices: Enrollment restrictions of type 'Device platform restrictions', configured to block 'Personally owned' for the Android platform
A device compliance policy that fails any device flagged as personally owned
A Conditional Access policy that blocks sign-ins from personally-owned devices
An app protection policy that blocks personally-owned devices from accessing corporate apps
questions.explanation: Enrollment restrictions (Devices → Enroll devices → Enrollment device platform restrictions) is the exact gate that decides which platform and ownership combinations are allowed to enroll. Setting the Android personally-owned option to Block stops enrollment before Intune ever creates a device record. Compliance policies only evaluate already-enrolled devices, so they are too late. Conditional Access controls access to cloud apps, not enrollment. App protection policies operate on app-level data, also after the device is in scope.

questions.q: What is the difference between an Intune COMPLIANCE policy and a CONFIGURATION profile?
choices: Compliance policies apply to Windows only, while configuration profiles cover all platforms
Compliance policies EVALUATE devices against requirements (and feed conditional access); configuration profiles CONFIGURE settings on the device
Configuration profiles run once at enrollment, while compliance policies re-apply settings hourly
They are functionally interchangeable — both enforce device settings, differing only in which portal blade is used to create and assign them to groups
questions.explanation: Compliance policies are assessments: they mark a device compliant/non-compliant against rules (encryption on, minimum OS, no jailbreak) and that verdict gates conditional access. Configuration profiles push actual settings. The pair works together — configure with profiles, verify with compliance — and both span platforms and re-evaluate continuously.

questions.q: An employee with a personally-owned, Intune-enrolled laptop is leaving. Corporate data and management must be removed while their personal files, apps and Windows installation remain intact. Which device action is correct?
choices: Wipe — restoring the laptop to factory settings, with all applications and user data removed from the disk
Autopilot Reset, reprovisioning the device for assignment to the next employee
Retire — removing managed apps, profiles and corporate data, then dropping Intune management
Fresh Start, which reinstalls Windows while preserving the enrollment state
questions.explanation: Retire is the BYOD exit: company apps, profiles, certificates and corporate data are removed and the device leaves management, while everything personal stays. Wipe factory-resets — destructive and inappropriate for personally-owned hardware; Autopilot Reset and Fresh Start rebuild corporate devices for reuse.

questions.q: Finance department laptops must receive a specific Autopilot deployment profile and app set automatically as soon as their hardware hashes are imported. What links the imported devices to the right profile?
choices: An Autopilot group tag on the imported devices, matched by a dynamic Entra device group the profile and apps are assigned to
Manually adding each device's serial number to a static Entra group after the box is unpacked and verified by a technician on site
The device naming template, which routes profiles based on the generated computer name
The primary user property, set during import to a finance department service account
questions.explanation: Group tags travel with the hardware hash (set at import or by the OEM); a dynamic device group with a rule like (device.devicePhysicalIds -any _ -contains "[OrderID]:Finance") picks the devices up instantly, and the deployment profile plus apps are assigned to that group. Static groups reintroduce manual handling; naming templates and primary user don't drive profile targeting.

questions.q: Security requires that every managed Windows device have a unique, automatically rotated local administrator password, retrievable by helpdesk from the cloud. What do you deploy?
choices: Windows LAPS via Intune account-protection policy, backing passwords up to Entra ID with rotation
A PowerShell platform script that sets one strong local administrator password, baked into the Autopilot deployment profile for all devices
Group Policy Preferences distributing the password from a share, as on legacy domains
Removal of all local administrator accounts so no local password exists to manage
questions.explanation: Windows LAPS is built into Windows and managed through Intune: per-device random passwords, scheduled rotation, escrow to Entra ID (or AD), and role-gated retrieval with auditing. One shared scripted password recreates the lateral-movement risk LAPS exists to kill — as does GPP password distribution (long deprecated for storing credentials readable in SYSVOL); removing local admin entirely breaks break-glass scenarios.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Helpdesk keeps fixing the same issue: a registry value reverting and breaking a line-of-business app on hundreds of devices. You want Intune to detect the bad state on a schedule and fix it automatically. Which feature fits?
flashcards.back: Remediations (formerly Proactive Remediations) run a detection script on a schedule and, when it returns non-compliant, execute the paired remediation script — purpose-built for recurring drift like registry reversions, with per-device reporting. App requirement rules gate installs; compliance policies flag rather than fix; Delivery Optimization is download peering, not repair.

flashcards.front: A zero-day is being exploited and Microsoft has released an out-of-band quality update. Update rings would wait days due to deferrals. How do you force critical patching now via Intune?
flashcards.back: Expedite policies override ring deferrals and pauses, pushing a named quality update with accelerated scan/install/restart handling and progress reporting — designed exactly for zero-day response. Zeroing deferrals still relies on normal scan cycles and user action; email attachments and re-imaging are not management at fleet scale.

flashcards.front: Branch offices with thin WAN links suffer when hundreds of devices each download the same multi-gigabyte feature update from the internet. Which technology reduces the duplicate WAN traffic?
flashcards.back: Delivery Optimization is the cloud-managed peer-to-peer cache for Windows Update (and Intune/Store content): set the download mode to LAN peering (optionally with a Connected Cache server) and each office pulls content from the internet roughly once. BranchCache predates and is superseded by DO for update content; Storage Sense and tunnel compression don't deduplicate downloads.

flashcards.front: A warehouse needs shared Windows devices that boot straight into a single inventory app and let users do nothing else. Which Intune configuration achieves this?
flashcards.back: Kiosk profiles configure Assigned Access: single-app mode locks the shell to one application above the lock screen — the standard pattern for warehouse scanners and signage. App protection policies govern data in apps, not the shell; compliance checks presence; hiding the Start menu still leaves the full desktop attack surface.

questions.q: Helpdesk keeps fixing the same issue: a registry value reverting and breaking a line-of-business app on hundreds of devices. You want Intune to detect the bad state on a schedule and fix it automatically. Which feature fits?
choices: Remediations — paired detection and remediation scripts run on a schedule
A Win32 app with a requirement rule re-deploying the application when detected as broken
A compliance policy marking affected devices non-compliant until helpdesk intervenes
Delivery Optimization rules re-downloading the app's content when corruption is found
questions.explanation: Remediations (formerly Proactive Remediations) run a detection script on a schedule and, when it returns non-compliant, execute the paired remediation script — purpose-built for recurring drift like registry reversions, with per-device reporting. App requirement rules gate installs; compliance policies flag rather than fix; Delivery Optimization is download peering, not repair.

questions.q: A zero-day is being exploited and Microsoft has released an out-of-band quality update. Update rings would wait days due to deferrals. How do you force critical patching now via Intune?
choices: An expedite quality update policy targeting the specific update to managed devices
Temporarily setting every ring's deferral to zero and asking users to check for updates
Emailing the standalone MSU package to users with installation instructions attached
Re-imaging affected devices with installation media that includes the new patch
questions.explanation: Expedite policies override ring deferrals and pauses, pushing a named quality update with accelerated scan/install/restart handling and progress reporting — designed exactly for zero-day response. Zeroing deferrals still relies on normal scan cycles and user action; email attachments and re-imaging are not management at fleet scale.

questions.q: Branch offices with thin WAN links suffer when hundreds of devices each download the same multi-gigabyte feature update from the internet. Which technology reduces the duplicate WAN traffic?
choices: Delivery Optimization with peer caching, letting devices on the local network share downloaded update content
BranchCache configured in distributed mode through legacy Group Policy objects applied to each branch office's organizational unit
Storage Sense policies that clear the update cache before each download begins
Compressing the VPN tunnel so update payloads consume fewer bytes in transit
questions.explanation: Delivery Optimization is the cloud-managed peer-to-peer cache for Windows Update (and Intune/Store content): set the download mode to LAN peering (optionally with a Connected Cache server) and each office pulls content from the internet roughly once. BranchCache predates and is superseded by DO for update content; Storage Sense and tunnel compression don't deduplicate downloads.

questions.q: A warehouse needs shared Windows devices that boot straight into a single inventory app and let users do nothing else. Which Intune configuration achieves this?
choices: A kiosk configuration profile in single-app mode running the inventory application
An app protection policy restricting data transfer out of the inventory app's context
A compliance policy requiring the inventory app to be present on every device
Removing the Start menu via a settings catalog policy so users cannot launch programs
questions.explanation: Kiosk profiles configure Assigned Access: single-app mode locks the shell to one application above the lock screen — the standard pattern for warehouse scanners and signage. App protection policies govern data in apps, not the shell; compliance checks presence; hiding the Start menu still leaves the full desktop attack surface.

questions.q: Security wants every Intune-managed Windows device automatically onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, with risk scores from MDE feeding device compliance. What establishes this integration?
choices: Enabling the Defender for Endpoint connector in Intune, deploying the MDE onboarding profile, and adding the machine-risk-score rule to compliance policy
Installing the Defender for Endpoint sensor manually from the security portal onto each device as part of the enrollment checklist
Configuring Windows Security baseline profiles, which include onboarding automatically
Federating the Defender portal with Entra ID so device objects synchronize risk attributes
questions.explanation: The Intune↔MDE connector (enabled on both sides) lets Intune push the EDR onboarding profile fleet-wide and consume MDE's machine risk score as a compliance-policy condition — which then drives conditional access. Manual sensor installs don't scale; security baselines harden settings but don't onboard MDE; there is no portal federation mechanism for this.

questions.q: An organization co-manages devices with Configuration Manager and Intune. They want Intune to take over ONLY Windows Update policies for a pilot group while ConfigMgr keeps everything else. Where is this controlled?
choices: Co-management workload sliders in the Configuration Manager console, moving the Windows Update workload to Intune for a pilot collection
Deleting the WSUS server so clients have no choice but to use Windows Update for Business
An Intune enrollment restriction that blocks ConfigMgr-managed devices from syncing policy
A Group Policy object that disables the Configuration Manager client agent on the pilot devices so Intune policies win every conflict
questions.explanation: Co-management workloads are switched individually (Pilot Intune → a chosen collection, then Intune fleet-wide): moving only Windows Update policies shifts that authority to Intune while ConfigMgr retains apps, baselines and the rest. Tearing down WSUS, blocking sync or disabling the agent are blunt actions that break management rather than transition a workload.
